Goal: I can connect slope to tangent of an angle and prove the parallel and perpendicular slope criteria with similar slope triangles (a 90 degree rotation for perpendicular).

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
For a line that rises from left to right, the slope equals tan θ, where θ is the angle the line makes with the positive x-direction.

Proof of the slope criteria. Parallel: parallel lines make equal corresponding angles with a horizontal line, so their slope triangles are similar by AA and the slopes are equal. Perpendicular: rotating a line 90 degrees turns its slope triangle with run a and rise b into a congruent triangle with run −b and rise a. So the slopes are b/a and −a/b, whose product is −1.

Each converse follows by running the argument backward. This closes the loop on 5.13.
